item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Nila has a weighing scale that is balanced, as in the diagram. The left pan holds one sealed packet and a $15\,\mathrm{g}$ weight. The right pan holds a $40\,\mathrm{g}$ weight.

How can she find the mass of the packet?

options.A: Remove the $15\,\mathrm{g}$ weight from the left pan only, then read the unbalanced pans as the packet mass.
options.B: The remaining comparison after removing equal weights from both pans is what first created the balanced pans.
options.C: Remove $15\,\mathrm{g}$ from both pans (take the $15\,\mathrm{g}$ weight off the left and replace the right $40\,\mathrm{g}$ with $25\,\mathrm{g}$), leaving the packet balanced against $25\,\mathrm{g}$.
options.D: Compare the pans while the scale is still tipped, using an unbalanced reading as the packet mass.
